notes.text: The source continues with a transitive system of isomorphisms between pi_t, used to identify all these groups with a common T, written literally à un =T. It calls the resulting angle-bracket object a T-groupoïde and explains that the fundamental groups of its connected components are commutative and all identified with T. No missing antecedent or preceding-page content is supplied.

The page says the extension group acts on this T-groupoid en opérant également sur T, through its actions on the pi-espace à gauche, on pi via autom int. of the extension group, and on T through G and chi. These are source statements; the reading également is supported by its initial accented e and descending g, and int. is not regularized to ext.

The lower bracketed paragraph restricts the action to pi, forms the action groupoid, assumes that groupoid abelian, and describes a family of abelian groups indexed by J equal to the round-labelled set modulo pi. The family notation (T_j) indexed by j in J is interlinear and retained as an insertion. The page says the extension-group action passes through its quotient G.

The final premise is written on suppose donné une trivialisation, with donné lacking the extra feminine e. It gives T simeq T_j and ends mid-phrase at compatible avec op. de. The opening square bracket remains unclosed on this sheet; no continuation or grammatical repair is added.

Both pencil numerals, 11 in the upper-right and 21 in the lower-left, are transcribed but their hand is unnamed. H’s phrase de l’auteur is editorial and is not used to attribute the pencil. The round tau/T label remains distinct from any earlier ornate Z, while E/Sigma remains the shared provisional notation at low confidence.

Complete second reading proposes no change. The candidate is a byte-for-byte copy of the accepted page. All 34 packet difference entries, all 37 accepted change rows, all three original MARKS and all eleven inventory items were checked; witness agreements were also read from the source.

The source describes a transitive identification of the pi_t with T and the resulting T-groupoid, then an action on the groupoid and on T. These statements were read as manuscript background, without proof verification or mathematical normalization.

The lower paragraph describes an abelian groupoid, a family indexed by the orbit quotient and an action through the extension-group quotient. The raised family notation is live; its conspicuous elbow belongs to the outer j rather than a securely distinct guide. No insertion-guide addition is proposed.

Abbreviations, literal two-bar shorthand, autom int., donné une, the four continuation points, the unclosed bracket and the incomplete final phrase are preserved. No change of the existing confidence metadata is proposed.

The existing two remaining-doubt entries are retained without narrowing: six E/Sigma graphs at low confidence and seven tau/calligraphic-T graphs at medium confidence. No new doubt or inventory element is added.
